CHAPTER V
SHORT-TERM USES OF THE ENVIRONMENT VERSUS LONG-TERM PRODUCTIVITY
A. The Balance Between Short-Term and Long-Term Effects
In summarizing the various environmental impacts that will result from the project action, it becomes apparent that the adverse effects will be of a short-term nature while the positive effects will benefit the Randolph area and residents on a long-run basis. The significant short-term impacts will occur during, but will not last beyond, the construction period in both the redevelopment and rehabilitation area. They include construction-associated impacts such as noise, dust, erosion and siltation, traffic disruption, and partially completed or demolished structures, streets or infrastructure components. More important will be the displacement over a period of time ofhundreds of families and several businesses throughout the demolition and redevelopment period. As discussed previously, however, sufficient relocation resources in the Richmond area have been shown to exist to accommodate relocatees and many are eventually expected to resettle in the Randolph neighborhood. (See Chapter II, Section B, Item 3.) Another relatively short-term effect is the length of the construction phase itself, expected to last several years. However, this period was planned to allow staging of new construction in order that displacees would be kept to a minimum at any one time and allowed to relocate back into new housing in Randolph as quickly as possible. The final negative impact will be the removal of street trees and disruption of recreation areas during construction. However, on completion of the project, not only will the trees have been replaced, but also the recreation area and open space within Randolph will be larger and of superior design.
There should be no significant long-term effects due to the project. The beneficial long-term effects, on the other hand, will be the following:
   The replacement of blight and substandard housing with a residential mix of rehabilitated housing and new residential construction.
2. The elimination of unsafe and hazardous living conditions for the project residents.
   A more efficient plan of land use in the area, particularly the design of open space areas.
4. The provision of improved infrastructure facilities. Proposed project improvements would include the existing street system, sanitary and storm sewer system, water system, gas distribution system, and power system.
